```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
urls <- c(
  "nzge.rds" = "https://phuongov.github.io/stats506-f26/data_f26/nzge.rds",
  "atp_matches_2019.csv" = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azhou5849/tennis-atp-sackmann-data/master/atp_matches_2019.csv",
  "us-states.csv" = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nytimes/covid-19-data/refs/heads/master/rolling-averages/us-states.csv"
)
for (filename in names(urls)) {
  destination <- file.path("data", filename)
  if (!file.exists(destination)) {
    download.file(urls[[filename]], destination, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  }
}

# Data loading
nzge <- readRDS("data/nzge.rds")
tennis <- read.csv("data/atp_matches_2019.csv")
covid <- read.csv("data/us-states.csv") |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
  filter(state %in% state.name) |>
  arrange(state, date)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
theme_update(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
             plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
             legend.position = "bottom")

```

## Problem 1(a)



```{r}
votes_by_year <- nzge |>
  group_by(election_year, voting_type) |>
  summarise(votes = sum(votes, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(votes))
kable(votes_by_year)

```

## Problem 1(b)

Percentages use all recorded Candidate votes as the denominator. Informal votes are shown explicitly; they are not a political party.

```{r}
# Informal votes are shown explicitly and are not interpreted as a political party.
candidate_2014 <- nzge |>
  filter(election_year == 2014, voting_type == "Candidate") |>
  group_by(party) |>
  summarise(votes = sum(votes, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(percent = 100 * votes / sum(votes)) |>
  arrange(desc(percent))
kable(candidate_2014, digits = 2)

```

## Problem 1(c)

The winner is the party with the greatest national vote total for each vote type, not necessarily the most seats.

```{r}
election_winners <- nzge |>
  filter(!grepl("^Informal", party)) |>
  group_by(election_year, voting_type, party) |>
  summarise(votes = sum(votes, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(election_year, voting_type) |>
  slice_max(votes, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(election_year) |>
  summarise(
    Candidate = paste(party[voting_type == "Candidate"], collapse = "; "),
    Party = paste(party[voting_type == "Party"], collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(election_year)
kable(election_winners)

```

## Problem 2(a)

A tournament is defined by a distinct `tourney_id`, including Davis Cup ties.

```{r}
tournament_count <- tennis |>
  summarise(tournaments = n_distinct(tourney_id))
kable(tournament_count)
cat(sprintf("The dataset contains %d distinct tournament IDs, including Davis Cup ties.\n",
            tournament_count$tournaments))

```

## Problem 2(b)

Individual singles titles are identified by final-round wins; Davis Cup team ties are excluded.

```{r}
titles <- tennis |>
  filter(round == "F", tourney_level != "D") |>
  distinct(tourney_id, winner_id, winner_name) |>
  count(winner_id, winner_name, name = "titles", sort = TRUE)
multiple_titles <- titles |> filter(titles > 1)
top_champions <- titles |> slice_max(titles, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE)
kable(multiple_titles)
kable(top_champions)
cat(sprintf("%d players won more than one singles tournament. %s each won %d titles.\n",
            nrow(multiple_titles), paste(top_champions$winner_name, collapse = " and "),
            max(titles$titles)))

```

## Problem 2(c)

This is a descriptive comparison of winner and loser ace counts within the same match. No hypothesis test is used.

```{r}
ace_pairs <- tennis |>
  filter(!is.na(w_ace), !is.na(l_ace)) |>
  mutate(difference = w_ace - l_ace)
ace_summary <- ace_pairs |>
  summarise(
    complete_matches = n(),
    winner_mean = mean(w_ace), loser_mean = mean(l_ace),
    mean_difference = mean(difference), median_difference = median(difference),
    winner_more_percent = 100 * mean(difference > 0),
    equal_percent = 100 * mean(difference == 0),
    loser_more_percent = 100 * mean(difference < 0)
  )
kable(ace_summary, digits = 2)
cat(sprintf(paste0("In %d complete pairs, winners averaged %.2f aces and losers %.2f; ",
                   "the mean paired difference was %.2f. Winners had more aces in %.1f%% ",
                   "of matches. This is descriptive evidence of an association, not ",
                   "a causal conclusion or a formal significance test. %d matches ",
                   "with missing ace statistics were excluded.\n"),
            nrow(ace_pairs), ace_summary$winner_mean, ace_summary$loser_mean,
            ace_summary$mean_difference, ace_summary$winner_more_percent,
            nrow(tennis) - nrow(ace_pairs)))

```

## Problem 2(d)



```{r}
player_records <- bind_rows(
  tennis |> transmute(player_id = winner_id, player = winner_name, win = 1L),
  tennis |> transmute(player_id = loser_id, player = loser_name, win = 0L)
) |>
  group_by(player_id) |>
  summarise(player = first(player), matches = n(), wins = sum(win),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(matches >= 5) |>
  mutate(win_rate = wins / matches)
best_players <- player_records |> slice_max(win_rate, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE)
kable(best_players |> mutate(win_percent = 100 * win_rate) |> select(-win_rate),
      digits = 2)
cat(sprintf("Among players with at least five matches, %s had the highest win rate: %.2f%%.\n",
            paste(best_players$player, collapse = "; "),
            100 * max(best_players$win_rate)))

```

## Problem 3(a)

Only the 50 states are included. Major and minor peaks are operational definitions, not official epidemiological classifications.

```{r}
#' Identify separated local peaks in a smoothed daily series.
#' @param y Numeric daily values, including possible NA edge values.
#' @param window Days examined on either side of each candidate peak.
#' @param minimum Minimum peak height.
#' @param separation Minimum distance in days between accepted peaks.
#' @return Integer indices of accepted peaks in chronological order.
find_peaks <- function(y, window = 30L, minimum = 20000, separation = 60L) {
  candidates <- integer()
  for (i in seq.int(window + 1L, length(y) - window)) {
    neighborhood <- y[(i - window):(i + window)]
    if (!anyNA(neighborhood) && y[i] >= minimum &&
        y[i] == max(neighborhood)) candidates <- c(candidates, i)
  }
  accepted <- integer()
  for (i in candidates[order(y[candidates], decreasing = TRUE)]) {
    if (all(abs(i - accepted) >= separation)) accepted <- c(accepted, i)
  }
  sort(accepted)
}

national <- covid |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(cases_avg = sum(cases_avg, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(date) |>
  mutate(smooth = as.numeric(stats::filter(cases_avg, rep(1 / 21, 21), sides = 2)))
peaks <- national |>
  slice(find_peaks(smooth)) |>
  mutate(type = if_else(smooth >= 100000, "Major", "Minor"))
kable(peaks |> select(date, smooth, type), digits = 0)
p3a <- ggplot(national, aes(date, smooth)) +
  geom_line(color = "#334155", linewidth = 0.7, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(data = peaks, aes(color = type), size = 2.8) +
  geom_text(data = peaks, aes(label = format(date, "%b %Y")),
            vjust = -0.8, size = 3, check_overlap = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Major = "#D55E00", Minor = "#0072B2")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.15))) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b\n%Y") +
  labs(title = "Waves of reported COVID-19 cases in the 50 states",
       subtitle = "NYT seven-day averages, smoothed with a centered 21-day mean",
       x = NULL, y = "Reported cases per day", color = "Peak class",
       caption = "Source: The New York Times. Major >=100,000; minor 20,000-99,999.\nLocal maxima within +/-30 days; peaks separated by >=60 days.")
print(p3a)
cat(sprintf("Under this operational definition, the plot contains %d major and %d minor peaks. Counts depend on the smoothing and thresholds; incomplete edge windows are excluded.\n",
            sum(peaks$type == "Major"), sum(peaks$type == "Minor")))

```

## Problem 3(b)

Overall rate means average daily reported cases per 100,000 over the common observation period. Equal observation periods make these rates comparable.

```{r}
coverage <- covid |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(first_day = min(date), last_day = max(date), .groups = "drop")
common_start <- max(coverage$first_day)
common_end <- min(coverage$last_day)
common <- covid |> filter(date >= common_start, date <= common_end)
state_rates <- common |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(overall_rate = mean(cases_avg_per_100k), .groups = "drop")
extreme_states <- bind_rows(
  state_rates |> slice_max(overall_rate, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE) |> mutate(group = "Highest"),
  state_rates |> slice_min(overall_rate, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE) |> mutate(group = "Lowest")
)
kable(extreme_states, digits = 2)
comparison <- common |> semi_join(extreme_states, by = "state")
p3b <- ggplot(comparison, aes(date, cases_avg_per_100k, color = state)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.65) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b\n%Y") +
  labs(title = "States with the highest and lowest overall reported incidence",
       subtitle = paste("Common observation period:", common_start, "to", common_end),
       x = NULL, y = "Daily cases per 100,000 (7-day average)", color = "State",
       caption = "Source: The New York Times. Overall rate = mean daily 7-day incidence.\nReported cases depend on testing and reporting practices.")
print(p3b)
trajectory_summary <- comparison |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(
    peak_rate = max(cases_avg_per_100k),
    peak_date = date[which.max(cases_avg_per_100k)],
    days_above_50 = sum(cases_avg_per_100k >= 50), .groups = "drop"
  )
kable(trajectory_summary, digits = 2)
cat(sprintf("%s had the highest overall rate and %s the lowest.\n",
            paste(extreme_states$state[extreme_states$group == "Highest"], collapse = "; "),
            paste(extreme_states$state[extreme_states$group == "Lowest"], collapse = "; ")))
cat(paste(sprintf("%s peaked at %.2f daily cases per 100,000 on %s and spent %d days at or above 50.",
                  trajectory_summary$state, trajectory_summary$peak_rate,
                  trajectory_summary$peak_date, trajectory_summary$days_above_50),
          collapse = " "),
    "The higher-rate state had a much taller peak and a longer period of high incidence; the peaks also occurred at different times.\n")

```

## Problem 3(c)

Substantial incidence means at least one daily reported case per 100,000 (7-day average) for seven consecutive days. Ties at fifth place are retained.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 7
early <- covid |>
  filter(date <= as.Date("2020-05-31")) |>
  group_by(state) |>
  arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(sustained = as.numeric(stats::filter(
    as.integer(cases_avg_per_100k >= 1), rep(1, 7), sides = 1
  )) == 7) |>
  ungroup()
onsets <- early |>
  filter(sustained) |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(onset = min(date) - 6, .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(onset, state)
first_states <- onsets |> slice_min(onset, n = 5, with_ties = TRUE)
kable(first_states)
p3c <- early |>
  semi_join(first_states, by = "state") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, cases_avg_per_100k)) +
  geom_line(color = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "#D55E00") +
  geom_vline(data = first_states, aes(xintercept = onset),
             linetype = "dotted", color = "#555555") +
  facet_wrap(~state, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  labs(title = "Early sustained COVID-19 outbreaks",
       subtitle = "First five states; any ties at fifth place are retained",
       x = "2020", y = "Daily cases per 100,000 (7-day average)",
       caption = "Source: The New York Times. Dashed line: 1 case per 100,000.\nDotted lines: start of the first 7-day run at or above that threshold.")
print(p3c)
cat(sprintf("Using the stated threshold, the earliest states were %s. These are dates of sustained reported incidence, not dates of first infection.\n",
            paste(first_states$state, collapse = ", ")))
```
